source.version_note: Published Frontiers in Psychology brief research report, volume11,article2011,30September2020. Article2011is an identifier, not the publication year. The supplied PDF includes Appendix1 with the complete25-item questionnaire.
source.verification_method: All twelve supplied pages, two figures, both tables, all references and all25 Appendix1items read. Stimulus images, five-panel outcome figure and corrupted Table2headers visually inspected. Crossref/publisher verify nine authors and date. Printed-summary sample/eta/contrast arithmetic checked; no raw-data replication. Selected bibliography identities verified through Crossref, without claiming full readings.

citation.title: A Robot Is Not Worth Another: Exploring Children’s Mental State Attribution to Different Humanoid Robots

reading.source_scope_note: Cross-sectional Italian children’s yes/no capacity attributions to paper images of a gender-matched human and one of two robot platforms. No live robot, actual AI reasoning, verified machine emotion, developmental intervention or direct measure of animism, uncanny feelings or false-belief performance. Mixed repeated-measures methods are described, with material reporting inconsistencies left unresolved.
access_limits: All twelve supplied pages read, including both figures, both tables and all25 Appendix1questions. Main stimulus and result figures and problematic table layout visually checked. Publisher HTML inspected for identity, availability and correction/supplement references. No supplied or publisher-listed supplementary file or corrigendum found in that bounded inspection.

Data availability says datasets are available on request. No public raw-data or analysis-code link, prospective registration, complete model output or exact collection dates verified. No author contacted. No child-level records or identifiers accessed.

The instrument portal is a generic website/Strumenti locator, while the full questionnaire is already reproduced in Appendix1. Its external portal, other versions and independent validation studies were not read. Published alpha coefficients are reported, not re-estimated.

Crossref identifies the extra DOI printed after Belpaeme2018as Beran and colleagues’2011 Understanding how children understand robots, rather than the2018educationreview. Correct review DOI10.1126/scirobotics.aat5954also verified. This is a wrong attached reference pointer, not a fabricated paper.

Crossref also verifies the cited Marchetti2020volume/authororder,DiDio2018journalclassification,andHackel2014volume. Metadata only: no independent full readings of these papers,Piaget’sbook or the developmental-robotics books. No full-paper Markdown copy, private access, author program or participant-data replication.

study.sample: 189 initially acquired Italian kindergarten/primary-school children:72inNAO,117inRobovie. Robovie is randomly subsampled to24,25,23children aged5,7,9respectively,matchingNAO’sagecounts;the described selected total is144. This is random subsampling, not documented random assignment to robot platform. Reported GLM residualdf126doesnot reconcile with a conventional complete144-person3×2×2between-factorial(df132)without further cases/model details.
study.design: One researcher tests children individually in a quiet school room for about10minutes. Each sees a gender-matched human drawing and either Robovie or NAO image; human/robot presentation order and five question-category order randomized. Robot identity,shape,legs/hands,face and possibly image medium are bundled. Chronological age is observed, not assigned, and cross-sectional groups are not longitudinal developmental change.
study.stimuli: Figure1shows line drawings of male/female humans and photographs of two robot platforms. NAO is classified as more human-like from prior sources; participants are not described as completing an independent physical-human-likeness manipulation check. No live behavior, adaptation or repeated interaction occurs.
study.instrument: AMS has25binary yes/no items in five categories of five:perceptive,emotive,intentions/desires,imaginative,epistemic. Total0–25,category0–5. Five category alphas.8,.8,.8,.8,.7andtotal.9reported. Perceptive items mix functional sensing and subjective hot/cold; epistemic items include understanding,decision,learning,teaching,thought. Imaginative includes lying,pretending,joking,dreaming. These are heterogeneous attributions, not validated separate mechanisms or objective capacity tests.
study.analysis: Stated GLM uses state(5)andagent(human/robot)within participants;age(3),gender(2),robotplatform(2)between participants. Greenhouse–Geisser correction for sphericity violations and Bonferroni posthoc comparisons are explicitly described. Do not characterize the entire analysis as independent-row pseudoreplication. Exact fitted sample/model,correctionepsilon and interaction output are unavailable.
study.reported_main_results: Human-versus-robotF1,126=570.9,partialeta².819;stateF4,504=40.33,eta².243;platformF1,126=39.4,eta².238. Agent×ageF2,126=25.17,eta².285. Those F/df/eta combinations approximately reconcile arithmetically. Overall humans receive greater ratings and NAO generally exceeds Robovie in reported contrasts; neither means every state/age contrast differs nor proves actual robot mentality.
study.interactions: Source reports state×agentF1,126=16.51,eta².183 andstate×age×platformF8,126=4.95,eta².073. These specific F/df/eta triplets do not reconcile:printed values implyeta²about.116and.239respectively. A hypothetical denominator504would produce.073for the latter, but that is a diagnostic, not a verified correction. Preserve the reported interaction claim with uncertainty rather than replace all statistics.
study.age_specific_pattern: Reported planned contrasts/figure show youngest children distinguishing NAO/Robovie mainly on perceptive and epistemic categories, older children on more categories, with imaginative platform differences not detected. Younger children’s NAO emotion attribution can be lower because fewer negative emotions are endorsed. Thus the headline younger-more-anthropomorphic pattern is not uniform across all states/platforms.
study.inference_limits: No measured animism scale or causal mediation supports the suggested animism explanation. No eerie-feeling scale or graded near-human continuum supports an uncanny-valley effect in this study. Higher human ratings are not an independent ToM-competence test or evidence that children know machines’ actual subjective states.
study.reporting: Table2lower columns contain negative values under standard-error/significance headings and look like interval endpoints; interval level is not given. Human age contrasts−.558,−.558and−.108cannot all describe the same marginal means. Reported human4.6minusrobot2.7doesnotyield the printed1.75difference;plotbars also require clarification. Do not reconstruct corrected means,pvalues or exclusions from these discrepancies.
study.scope: School children not reported by parents/teachers for learning or social difficulties; that report is not an independently assessed clinical diagnosis. Parental written consent and local ethics approval reported. No autism intervention,actual educational benefit,optimal robot design,privacy outcome,acceptance behavior or moral-status judgment is tested.

summary: No new row. Enrich existing mind perception,anthropomorphism,experience attribution and agency attribution with the full child questionnaire and bounded image-rating evidence. Add non-counted animism,mentalizing and uncanny-valley context. Record sample/model/table inconsistencies and wrong bibliography pointers without inventing a repaired dataset or developmental mechanism.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: The full25-item yes/no AMS questionnaire measures attributed perceptive,emotive,intentional,imaginative and epistemic capacities for paper targets. State,age and platform patterns are reported in a repeated-measures design,with uncertainty from inconsistent output.
findings.boundary: AMS dimensions are questionnaire content,not five independent behaviors or proof of universal mental structure. Attributions are not verified actual capacity,sentience,personhood or accurate ToM. Cross-sectional age differences and bundled platform images do not identify developmental causes.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: The source operationalizes psychological anthropomorphism through capacity attributions and compares two pictured humanoid platforms. NAO generally receives higher attribution in reported contrasts; pattern differs by age/state.
findings.boundary: Image-based attribution is not live interaction,preference,trust or actual human-like capacity. Two platforms change multiple features and lack documented randomized platform assignment. Do not generalize to all mechanical/human-like robots or assume maximizing anthropomorphism benefits children.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: Appendix1includes attributed feelings and sensations:anger,fear,happiness,surprise,sadness and hot/cold. Younger children’s lower NAO negative-emotion endorsement qualifies a uniform younger-more-experience interpretation.
findings.boundary: Endorsing a binary feeling question does not establish actual robot sensation,accurate ontology or a child’s clinical/social competence. Affective valence and total mental-attribution score differ; the source’s posthoc negative-emotion chi-square notation lacks enough output for independent inference.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: Intention,wanting,willingness,wishes,preferences and epistemic decisions are directly queried. Attributions depend on image platform,age and item group in reported contrasts,not actual observed autonomous action.
findings.boundary: A child’s willingness to ascribe planning or preference is not verified robotic agency,authority,moral responsibility or a separate causal mental dimension. The questionnaire does not test the target’s ability to execute those capacities.

findings.definition: Attributing life, vitality or a soul to nonhuman entities, including objects or features of nature.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion proposes animistic interpretation of inanimate things as an explanation for younger children’s broad robot attributions,using prior developmental literature.
findings.boundary: Context only:animism or biological category confusion is not independently measured here. Do not label every robot attribution,false-belief response,metaphor or cultural/spiritual belief an error. Do not infer a mediator or a universal age cutoff from this cross-sectional task.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: The background defines reasoning about mental states,and future work calls for direct language,executive-function and ToM measures. The present task collects attributions rather than independently testing false-belief understanding.
findings.boundary: Context only. High human-target scores are not a validated ToM assessment or proof of accurate private-state inference. Do not diagnose children,claim tested model mentalizing or equate all anthropomorphism with successful theory of mind.

findings.definition: A drop in comfort or affinity when an artificial agent appears highly, but imperfectly, human-like, rather than a steady increase as human likeness rises.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use existing mental-capacity attribution and anthropomorphism records. Questionnaire dimensions, a proposed animism explanation and a two-robot comparison do not supply independent new behaviors or ethical principles.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion invokes prior uncanny-valley literature to qualify the recommendation for human/mechanical design combinations.
findings.boundary: Context only:no eerie-feeling outcome or graded near-human continuum is measured. A two-platform rating difference cannot establish a nonmonotonic valley,optimal design point or universal child discomfort.

source_corrections.finding: Columns labeled standard error and significance contain negative values and pairs resembling lower/upper interval bounds. Such numbers cannot be standard errors or p values. Preserve reported contrasts but treat those column labels as corrupted; do not infer an unreported confidence level or copy endpoints as significance.

The appended DOI10.1016/j.ijhcs.2011.04.003identifies Beran/Ramirez-Serrano/Kuzyk/Fior/Nugent2011 Understanding how children understand robots:Perceived animism in child–robot interaction,not Belpaeme2018 Social robots for education:A review. Retain the verified correct review DOI10.1126/scirobotics.aat5954and detach the unrelated pointer. Both works exist; original works unread.
The cited DOI belongs to Frontiers in Psychology11:2245,notvolume10. Crossref author order is Marchetti,DiDio,Massaro,Manzi rather than Manzi before Massaro. Metadata correction only.
Growing Up Thinking of God’s Beliefs is a Sage Open8(4)journalarticle,not a location/publisher book-style reference. Use its verified journal identity and resolving DOI; no full-study credit.
Journal of Experimental Social Psychology volume is52,pages15–23. The printed2014in the volume position is the year,not the actual volume. Preserve the correct2014publication year and DOI.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Described selected age cells sum to144,whereas repeated denominator126doesnot match the conventional full3×2×2between-factorial residual132. Missing cases,covariates or a different model could change degrees of freedom,but none is documented sufficiently. Exact analyzed N and formula remain unverified; do not silently declare138or144complete GLM cases.

State×agentF16.51with1,126impliespartialeta²≈.116rather than.183. Three-wayF4.95with8,126implies≈.239rather than.073;denominator504would approximately produce.073but is not verified. Other reported F/eta combinations reconcile,so do not describe every effect as arithmetically invalid.

HumanM4.6androbotM2.7do not yield Mdiff1.75even allowing ordinary one-decimal rounding. Figure2shows many robot bars near3–4rather than a uniform2.7pattern. Human5vs7and5vs9both−.558implyzero7vs9difference,not−.108. Exact means/conditioning and corrected entries require source outputs; no plot digitization or fabricated repairs.

In the stated design,Robotplatform is a between-person factor while Human/Robot agent is within person. A main platform effect normally averages over both agents unless conditioned further. The report does not show enough marginal-output detail to determine whether M3.98/3.4are conditional robot-only means or broader averages. Do not relabel them as independently verified direct robot-specific effects.

Some reciprocal comparisons have different printed standard errors or adjusted significance,including perceptive/imaginative and epistemic/imaginative directions. Reversing a matched contrast should reverse its sign without changing its uncertainty or two-sided inference under the same adjustment. Exact output is unavailable; do not choose one direction’s number as repaired truth.

Discussion writes chi-square<.01without statistic,df,counts or an unambiguous p value. It cannot independently establish the claimed significance. Retain the reported valence explanation as exploratory without converting that notation into a verified p<.01result.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The source explicitly specifies repeated within-person state/agent factors,Greenhouse–Geisser correction and Bonferroni comparisons. Reporting inconsistencies warrant targeted clarification,not a blanket assertion that all observations were treated as independent.

Age-related interactions and a three-way interaction are explicitly reported. Their exact numerical reporting has limits,but the paper does not rely solely on significance in one subgroup versus nonsignificance in another.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All robot participants were randomly assigned
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Random subsampling of the larger Robovie sample and randomized presentation order are documented. Random assignment to robot platform is not documented; these are different operations.
The tables print three-decimal significance entries. Interpret .000as below the display threshold rather than a literal probability of zero.

Failure to detect a NAO/Robovie imaginative-score difference and generally higher human ratings do not prove universal absence of machine imagination or equivalent robot scores. The task measures beliefs rather than objective capability.

methodological_limits: Cross-sectional age groups and nonverified platform assignment do not identify causal development or isolate appearance. Random presentation/subsampling and repeated-measures methods address specific issues without eliminating all confounding.

Two fixed platforms and drawn human versus photographed robot stimuli bundle identity,appearance and medium. Broader cultures,platforms and live interactions remain future work acknowledged by the source.

AMS mixes functional sensory abilities,subjective feelings,intention and epistemic/imaginative judgments. A total score or alpha is not a consciousness test,validated child competence diagnosis or proof of an objective psychological mechanism.

Preserve reported formal interactions and appropriate repeated design,while flagging sample/df/effect-size/contrast inconsistencies. Exact corrected statistics cannot be manufactured from the current tables or approximate graph heights.

Animism is an unmeasured explanation; uncanny valley,trust,education,friendship and successful ToM are not direct outcomes. Do not turn background theory or design recommendations into new observed effects.
Younger-more-anthropomorphic is an overall source interpretation with state-specific exceptions,including NAO negative-emotion attributions. It is not a uniform pattern for every item,age and robot.
Higher human-target scores do not prove accurate knowledge about the pictured robots. Human rights and a child’s worth never depend on these ratings; school/clinical extrapolations are unsupported.

Data are on request and no author contacted. Printed-summary arithmetic and verified citation metadata are limited checks,not raw-data replication,independent instrument validation or intent attribution.

cross_paper_learning.finding: That prospective belief scale and this child target-rating questionnaire are different measures. Neither factor labels nor age differences establish five new principles,universal trait structure or machine feeling.

Keep an image-based attribution association distinct from a within-person capacity-description intervention. Both need source-specific outcome and inference boundaries rather than an undifferentiated anthropomorphism effect.

A child’s attribution to a picture is not proof of intentionally misleading robot behavior. Superficial-state deception needs verified capacity truth and a misleading signal,not an attribution score alone.

Existing Animism covers broader attribution of life/vitality and cultural meanings. The developmental animism-error explanation here is contextual and unmeasured; do not redefine all animism as pathological or mistaken.
A five-category questionnaire is not an independently discovered five-factor mental structure. Distinguish planned item groupings,aggregate target ratings and validated individual latent dimensions.

deferred.term: Five AMS dimensions as five new behaviors
deferred.reason: Questionnaire item categories,not independent new named behaviors. Existing mind/agency/experience records cover the underlying attributions.

deferred.term: Animism error as a newly demonstrated mechanism
deferred.reason: A proposed explanation drawn from prior literature; no direct animism or category-confusion measure here. Preserve as non-counted context under Animism.
Posthoc valence interpretation without a separately defined/validated construct or complete chi-square output; no new name invented.
Two picture platforms and attribution ratings do not establish optimality,live educational benefit,trust or safety.

limitations: No new rows; four existing records enriched with directly relevant questionnaire evidence and three with non-counted context. Catalogue stays771records in eleven categories,with stable IDs and unnumbered rows. Seven evaluation criteria and six principles unchanged. No fabricated source totals,annual counts,clinical findings,full-paper Markdown archive or independent replication claim.
